newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-firm - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-firm - dealers.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices Monday were seen steady with a firm tone, amid expectations for continued light hog supplies, livestock dealers said.
The light supplies were seen offsetting potential bearishness from planned slaughter reductions early next week by several meat packing companies, they said.

IBP Thursday announced it was trimming operating hours at virtually all its seven pork plants through next week. Excel also announced reduced hours but did not say which of their three hog plants would be affected or for how long.

Top prices for hogs delivered to the plant Monday in Iowa and southern Minnesota could range from $55.50 to $56.00 per cwt. Illinois top plant prices could range from $54.00 to $55.00. Indiana/Ohio top hog prices at the plant could range from $53.50 to $55.00, livestock dealers said.
Light hog supplies were resulting in reduced pork production, with this week's level at 328.9 million pounds, down 3.4 percent from the previous week and 12.9 percent below a year ago, USDA said.
